3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: Meanwhile, Gus Manger had invited me to visit the Gasom headquarters in Narbel. It was situated in Ornobel, a neighborhood on the city outskirts.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: Next to it was the Damenoy gas reserve, a prominent natural gas source consisting of four large fields.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: The roads were bumpy and marked by potholes, while the buildings surrounded us appeared run-down and dilapidated. The community had apparently endured a prolonged period of neglect.

6.speaker: Narrator
6.text: We came to a halt at the entrance gates of the facility. A sizeable mural depicting the Gasom logo had been painted on a nearby wall.

7.speaker: Narrator
7.text: After a series of intense meetings with Ciara and Paskal, I decided to take some much-needed time to recharge.

17.speaker: Narrator
17.text: I checked in with Lucian and Petr back at the capital. They were working hard to unite democratically leaning reformers for the crucial task of drafting a new constitution.

18.speaker: Narrator
18.text: I checked in with Lucian and Petr back at the capital. They had devoted themselves to the challenging task of uniting pro-centralization factions behind the drafting of a new constitution.

19.speaker: Narrator
19.text: I checked in with Lucian and Petr back at the capital. They were engaged in intense negotiations with the Old Guard in order to address their pressing national security concerns.
19.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Autocrat_Path"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Dictator_Path"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Reformist_Path"] == true) == false)

20.speaker: Narrator
20.text: I checked in with Lucian and Petr back at the capital. They were working tirelessly, exploring all possibilities and avenues to advance the constitutional reform draft.
20.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Autocrat_Path"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Dictator_Path"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Reformist_Path"] == true) == false)

21.speaker: Narrator
21.text: Ewald Alphonso stood up from his chair. He had on a perfectly tailored suit that he wore as casually as pajamas.

23.speaker: Narrator
23.text: Adjacent to the mural, a group of individuals wearing blue work vests had assembled, holding what looked like protest signs.

24.speaker: Gus Manger
24.text: "Good day, President Rayne. Welcome to Gasom's Narbel operations!"

25.speaker: Gus Manger
25.text: “It takes one to know one. As promised, I've brought our guest of honor.”

26.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
26.text: “President Rayne. I hope you enjoyed seeing our facilities here.”

27.speaker: Player
27.text: “President Alphonso. It's nice to see what you have built from the inside.”

28.speaker: Player
28.text: “The facilities appear to be in much better shape than the city around them.”

29.speaker: Player
29.text: “Greetings. I'm curious to find out more about where Gasom stands.”

30.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
30.text: “It's fine. Nothing compared to the Gasom HQ in Holsord, of course."

31.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
31.text: "You should have seen Narbel before Gasom came here. The jobs it generated have had a lasting positive effect."

32.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
32.text: "The same sentiment applies to the government's stance on our energy policy."

33.speaker: Gus Manger
33.text: “Still one of the standouts of the Maroon District.”

34.speaker: Gus Manger
34.text: "It's true. Things here could be a lot worse."

35.speaker: Gus Manger
35.text: “Plenty of discussions we can have. We have the two new faces of Sordland in one room. The old man is nowhere to be seen.”

36.speaker: Narrator
36.text: We sat down. Some snacks and drinks were served. Multiple Gasom yearly financial reports were scattered on the table between us.

38.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
38.text: “If we raise a minority investment, it would allow us to invest in further resource excavations in the gas fields, and turn the company back to significant profitability.”

39.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
39.text: “By significant, I mean that our projections show that we would be able to cover eighty percent of Sordland's gas needs in three years, and we would achieve profits four times the value of our investment.”

40.speaker: Player
40.text: "If we are to invest in Gasom, I want to make sure that the company is also committed to improving the socio-economic conditions in Narbel."

41.speaker: Player
41.text: "Your projections sound impressive. However, we need to consider the international market as well. How do we plan to compete against nations like Anraka, Arcasia, United Contana?"

42.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
42.text: "I understand your concern. The risk is indeed there, but our experienced team of geologists and engineers have identified promising fields."

43.speaker: Gus Manger
43.text: "Ewald's got a point, Mr. President. Sure, there's some risk, but look at the upside -- Sordland could be energy resilient. I reckon that's a gamble worth taking, especially in these tough economic times."

44.speaker: Narrator
44.text: Ewald walked back over to the window. He stood there, silhouetted against the vast expanse of the gas fields.

45.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
45.text: "I wholeheartedly agree. The well-being of Narbel's citizens is a priority for Gasom."

46.speaker: Player
46.text: "An enticing proposition. However, I would like to know more about the risks involved. What if the excavations do not yield the expected results?"

53.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
53.text: "Your attitude and choices as President has prompted me to reflect on the significant gap that exists between us. Regrettably, this divide could pose challenges to the feasibility of any prospective business collaboration."

54.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
54.text: "Mr. President, I believe we have the potential for a mutually beneficial partnership. However, we need to align our objectives and expectations."

59.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
59.text: "We've got a strong strategy in place. Our competitive edge lies in the quality and efficiency of our production."

60.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
60.text: "The odds are in our favor. And let's not forget the potential rewards are substantial."

61.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
61.text: "With this investment, we could certainly allocate some funds to improve the local infrastructure and create more jobs."

62.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
62.text: "With this investment, we can further enhance our technologies and stay ahead of the competition."

63.speaker: Gus Manger
63.text: "Mr. President, I've been thinking -- what if we tie Gasom's growth to Narbel's development? Get the company to invest in the community, you know? That way, everybody wins."

64.speaker: Gus Manger
64.text: "Ewald and his team have been doing a hell of a job. Give them the right backing, and I reckon Gasom could give the big boys a run for their money. We just need to have a little faith."

68.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
68.text: "Mr. President, your administration's focus on a planned economy resonates with our strategic vision."

69.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
69.text: "Mr. President, your administration's commitment to a market economy aligns with our vision for a competitive corporation."

70.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
70.text: "A government investment in our company aligns perfectly with this approach. It's about strengthening Sordland's economy and becoming self-sufficient in energy production."

71.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
71.text: "With a government investment, we can further liberalize the energy market, enhance our technologies, and compete globally."

72.speaker: Player
72.text: "The Kingdom of Rizia's investment would reduce the risk for us. However, we need to carefully consider the implications of sharing control with a foreign entity."

73.speaker: Player
73.text: "I'm heavily interested in the idea of Gasom investing in Narbel's development. But we need concrete actions, not just words."

74.speaker: Player
74.text: "I see the potential for us to drive Sordland's energy independence. But we need to make sure this is a sustainable solution."

75.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
75.text: "You bring up a valid point. We're dedicated to responsible resource extraction and have allocated a portion of the proposed investment for environmental mitigation measures."

76.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
76.text: "The partnership with Rizia is indeed a new venture for us, as a company, Anton. However, they have a vested interest in a stable gas supply."

77.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
77.text: "You're right to demand specifics. With this investment, we aim to improve the living conditions in Narbel by creating more jobs, providing better housing for our workers, and initiating educational programs."

78.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
78.text: "Sustainability is a key part of our strategy."

79.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
79.text: "Our agreement would be focused on operations and profits, but not policy – Gasom would remain under Sordish control."

80.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
80.text: "Gasom is as committed to Narbel as it is to Sordland."

81.speaker: Gus Manger
81.text: "Couldn't agree more, Mr. President. We've got to keep the big picture in mind, and that includes our environment. I trust Ewald and his team to handle this responsibly."

82.speaker: Gus Manger
82.text: "Mr. President, I know the Rizians want the same thing we do. And the more energy partners we have, the better off we'll be. Plus, we'll keep the reins on Gasom."

83.speaker: Gus Manger
83.text: "It's about time Narbel got a leg up. Ewald's plan sounds solid to me. More jobs, better living conditions – that's a step in the right direction."

84.speaker: Player
84.text: "We'll co-invest with Rizia. We'll share the costs and stakes." [-1 Government Budget]

85.speaker: Player
85.text: "We won't invest at this time. Let the Kingdom and other foreign investors contribute."

86.speaker: Player
86.text: "We're investing alone. Sordland will provide the majority of funds, and Gus will tell Rizia to back off." [-2 Government Budget]

87.speaker: Narrator
87.text: After a moment, he turned back to face us. His gaze was steady, the expectation clear in his eyes. The time had come to make a decision.

91.speaker: Gus Manger
91.text: "Before we dive into the celebrations, I've allocated time during this meeting for President Rayne to discuss any concerns regarding Gasom's treatment of its workers and its effects on Narbel."

92.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
92.text: "Your decision shows a commitment to Sordland's energy independence. We won't let you down."

93.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
93.text: "A joint investment? A wise choice. It ensures steady funds for Gasom."

94.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
94.text: "I understand your reservations. We'll continue to serve Sordland's energy needs."

95.speaker: Gus Manger
95.text: "That's a bold move, Mr. President. But I reckon it's the right one. Gasom's success will be Sordland's success."

96.speaker: Gus Manger
96.text: "I like the way you think, Mr. President. Sharing the costs with Rizia reduces our risk and strengthens our ties. It's a smart move."

97.speaker: Gus Manger
97.text: "Well, Mr. President, you've always been one to play it safe. I guess we'll just have to make do and see how things turn out."

98.speaker: Player
98.text: "The wages of Gasom blue-collar workers need to be increased. They are the backbone of your operations."

99.speaker: Player
99.text: "I expect Gasom to contribute significantly to local charities, to aid in the city's recovery."

100.speaker: Player
100.text: "The workers of Gasom need better housing, access to healthcare, and opportunities for education. As the leading industry there, Gasom can't ignore its responsibility."

101.speaker: Player
101.text: "We've covered a lot today. I believe we can wrap up the meeting now."

102.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
102.text: "President Rayne, I appreciate your concerns about Narbel. Rest assured, we are constantly evaluating our impact on the community and are looking for ways to improve."

103.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
103.text: "Mr. President, while I acknowledge your concerns, Gasom's primary responsibility is to its shareholders and the economic stability of Sordland."

104.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
104.text: "A good point. I see the potential for Gasom to play a larger role in supporting our workers and the community."

123.speaker: Gus Manger
123.text: "It's been a long day. We've got a lot to think about."

124.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
124.text: "President Rayne, the welfare of our workers is certainly important. We'll continue to review their conditions and remuneration."

125.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
125.text: "Mr. President, while I understand your concerns, we must consider the financial implications of such actions. I cannot really promise you anything."

126.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
126.text: "I fully agree that we must do more for our workers. Their welfare is a priority for Gasom."

127.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
127.text: "President Rayne, I understand the role Gasom could play in supporting local charities."

128.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
128.text: "Mr. President, Gasom already contributes significantly to Sordland's economy."

129.speaker: Gus Manger
129.text: "Well, this is promising. Ewald's commitment to these initiatives should alleviate some of our concerns."

130.speaker: Gus Manger
130.text: "Gentlemen, it's clear that we all share the goal of improving the situation in Narbel. Let's continue working together to make that happen."

131.speaker: Gus Manger
131.text: "We're all in agreement that we should do more for the local community. Let's move forward with that in mind."

132.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
132.text: "I will personally oversee initiatives to provide private housing, health, and education support for our blue-collar workers."

133.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
133.text: "I will personally ensure that we review their salaries and work towards providing them with competitive compensation immediately."

134.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
134.text: "I share your concerns about Narbel. Gasom is committed to implementing sustainable practices that will lessen our impact on the environment and the community."

135.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
135.text: "Personally, I am committed to supporting local charities to enhance our community engagement."

136.speaker: Player
136.text: "That's reassuring to hear. I trust that you'll follow through on these commitments."

137.speaker: Player
137.text: "These are significant steps. I look forward to seeing these changes implemented swiftly."

138.speaker: Player
138.text: "Agreed, Gus. Mr. Alphonso, we expect to see tangible improvements in this city."

139.speaker: Player
139.text: "Gus, all the talk in the world won't change the situation in Narbel. We need concrete action from Gasom."

140.speaker: Gus Manger
140.text: "Ewald, your personal commitment to these initiatives speaks volumes. This could be a turning point for Gasom and for Narbel."

141.speaker: Narrator
141.text: Suddenly, the meeting was interrupted. The quiet murmur of a conversation from outside the room grew louder, followed by the sound of hurried footsteps.

145.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
145.text: "Gentlemen, it seems we have an unexpected situation outside. Some protestors from the Labor Union have blocked the main vehicular exits."

146.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
146.text: "We are not blind to the socio-economic conditions here. We're deeply invested in this community and are committed to doing our part."

147.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
147.text: "It's a challenging task to balance the needs of our shareholders with our responsibilities. I cannot promise you anything."

148.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
148.text: "We understand the importance of fair compensation. Discussions are ongoing on how to best support our hardworking employees. That is all I can say for the time being."

149.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
149.text: "We must indeed be mindful of the economic realities. We are striving to make decisions that are financially sound and sustainable."

150.speaker: Gus Manger
150.text: "Both of you make good points. It's a fine line between fulfilling our responsibilities and ensuring economic stability."

151.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
151.text: "Donating more is an interesting idea. It's something we will consider."

152.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
152.text: "Our contributions to Sordland's economy are substantial. Our focus must remain on maintaining that."

153.speaker: Player
153.text: "Indeed Gus, we have to ensure that we don't jeopardize the economic stability of Sordland. But we also can't ignore the plight of Narbel."

154.speaker: Player
154.text: "It's a fine line indeed. But that doesn't absolve us, or Gasom, of our responsibilities towards the people of Narbel."

155.speaker: Player
155.text: "That's true. And I hope that Gasom is ready to make some significant changes."

156.speaker: Player
156.text: "We're all in agreement, Gus. Now it's time to turn that agreement into action."

158.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
158.text: "We understand the need for action, Mr. President, but also--"

159.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
159.text: "As I mentioned before, we're always considering how we can--"

160.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
160.text: "Mr. President, I assure you that Gasom takes its responsibilities--"

161.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
161.text: "I understand, Anton. At Gasom, we are committed to reducing harm and contributing to the--"

162.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
162.text: "I agree, it's time for us to--"

163.speaker: Gus Manger
163.text: "We are all on the same page here. Let's not lose sight of that as we move forward."

164.speaker: Player
164.text: "I'm relieved to hear that. A fair wage is the least we can provide for the hardworking people of this country."

165.speaker: Player
165.text: "Promises are a start, Ewald. But the people need actions, not words. I look forward to seeing concrete changes."

166.speaker: Gus Manger
166.text: "Ewald, your personal commitment to these initiatives speaks volumes. This could be a turning point for Gasom and for Narbel."

167.speaker: Gus Manger
167.text: "This is still promising. Ewald's commitment to these initiatives should alleviate some of our concerns."

168.speaker: Player
168.text: "We need to do more than reduce harm. Our goal should be a better Narbel, not just a less bad one."

169.speaker: Player
169.text: "Charitable donations are commendable. But we must address the source of the harm, not just mitigate its effects."

170.speaker: Gus Manger
170.text: "I couldn't agree more. It's high time we took our responsibilities to Narbel seriously."

171.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
171.text: "Of course, we are fully committed to ensuring our operations are-"

178.speaker: Narrator
178.text: He approached Alphonso and leaned in to whisper something in his ear. Ewald nodded solemnly, his gaze meeting mine with a serious intensity.
178.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Gasom_LargeSordlandInvestmentAlone"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Gasom_CoInvestmentRizia"] == true)  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn03_EnT_Gasom_AlphonsoDealPoint"] >= 3) and (((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Gasom_LargeSordlandInvestmentAlone"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Gasom_CoInvestmentRizia"] == true)  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn03_EnT_Gasom_AlphonsoDealPoint"] >= 3) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Gasom_CoInvestmentRizia"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Gasom_OnlyRiziaInvestment"] == true)  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn03_EnT_Gasom_AlphonsoDealPoint"] >= 0) and (((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Gasom_CoInvestmentRizia"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Gasom_OnlyRiziaInvestment"] == true)  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn03_EnT_Gasom_AlphonsoDealPoint"] >= 0) == false)

179.speaker: Gus Manger
179.text: "Well, that's a pickle. What's our move, Ewald?"

180.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
180.text: "I have a helicopter ready. We can leave undetected and avoid the chaos and potential danger."

181.speaker: Serge Wolkner
181.text: "Mr. President, I have discussed the situation with the Presidential Guard and the police security. They are advising us not to go out the way we came in."

184.speaker: Serge Wolkner
184.text: "You must make a decision, Mr. President."

185.speaker: Narrator
185.text: As our motorcade made its way through the Ornobel district, I noted the neighborhood's state of disrepair.

186.speaker: Narrator
186.text: Serge skillfully parked the car, bringing our journey to a smooth and elegant conclusion. Gus greeted us warmly as we stepped out of the vehicle.

188.speaker: Player
188.text: "That's a shame. I still believe there's potential for us to work together in some capacity."

189.speaker: Player
189.text: "I understand, Mr. Alphonso. It's important that we each stay true to our principles."

190.speaker: Player
190.text: "Perhaps it's for the best, Mr. Alphonso. Your approach to business doesn't align with my vision for Sordland."

191.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
191.text: "We each have our roles to play for Sordland. Let us each do what we believe is right."

192.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
192.text: "I appreciate your optimism, Mr. President. While this particular deal may not have worked out, I remain open to future collaborations that could benefit both our interests and Sordland."

193.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
193.text: "Indeed, Mr. President. Our principles are what guide us."

197.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
197.text: "As a further gesture of goodwill, would you consider making a personal donation to the Alphonso Foundation? It's a cause close to my heart, focusing on providing shelter for the homeless in Sordland."

198.speaker: Player
198.text: "Gentlemen, after careful consideration, I've decided to step away from this deal." [No Deal Path]

199.speaker: Player
199.text: "Alright, let's proceed with the deal. The EPA restrictions will remain as they are, and I'll personally contribute to your cause for the homeless." [Deal Path, -1 Personal Wealth]

201.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
201.text: "If they don't point us in the same direction, then it's best we part ways here. I wish you all the best in your endeavors for Sordland."

203.speaker: Gus Manger
203.text: "You're right, Mr. President. There's always potential for collaboration. Let's not close the door just yet."

204.speaker: Gus Manger
204.text: "Wait. Gentlemen, let's not let a single disagreement define our relationship. There's a bigger picture here."

205.speaker: Gus Manger
205.text: "I understand that tensions are high right now. But I have faith that we can find a solution that benefits everyone."

206.speaker: Gus Manger
206.text: "However, for that to happen, I need to know: Mr. President, do you trust my judgement?"

207.speaker: Player
207.text: "Gus, I respect you, but I can't trust your judgement in this matter. You seem to have a fundamental bias on this." [Reject Deal]

208.speaker: Player
208.text: "I trust your advice. You've proven yourself a reliable ally and I believe we can find a way forward."

209.speaker: Player
209.text: "Your judgement has been questionable at times. But I'm willing to hear you out."

210.speaker: Gus Manger
210.text: "Thank you, Mr. President. I propose a compromise."

211.speaker: Gus Manger
211.text: "If you promise not to tighten the current restrictions of the Energy Protection Act, we can reconsider our stance and keep the deal on the table."

212.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
212.text: "Mr. President, I'm giving you a chance to prove your commitment to the people of Sordland and to our shared future."

213.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
213.text: "I hope you'll consider our offer carefully. This could be the beginning of a fruitful partnership, or the end of a potential alliance."

214.speaker: Gus Manger
214.text: "Fair enough, Mr. President. I gave it my all."

215.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
215.text: "We both tried, it seems. Still, I appreciate the discussion, Mr. President."

216.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
216.text: "Well, Mr. President? Will Gasom and Sordland make history or not?"

217.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
217.text: "Mr. Rayne, the foundation for a robust partnership is right here. It's high time we shift our focus towards sealing this deal."

218.speaker: Player
218.text: "You've made a compelling case. Let's get this deal on the road. I can assure you that the EPA restrictions won't get any stricter." [Deal Path]

220.speaker: Gus Manger
220.text: "I'm glad you're on board, Mr. President."

224.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
224.text: "If the Sordish government chooses to invest, it would gain a voice in the broader company decisions, even as a minority stakeholder."

225.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
225.text: "The government could either liquidate its shares at a future date or continue to reap the long-term profits."

227.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
227.text: "Excellent, Mr. President! Your support for the homeless cause is commendable. Together, we will ensure a promising future for Gasom."

228.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
228.text: "Mr. President, your assurances on the EPA front are much appreciated. This partnership is going to bring great benefits for all."

229.speaker: Gus Manger
229.text: "You know, Mr. President, if we can get the government in on this, it's a win-win."

230.speaker: Gus Manger
230.text: "Not only does Gasom continue to operate and grow, but it also strengthens the state's energy security and economic power. We just need a little risk appetite, that's all."

231.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
231.text: "Are you ready, Mr. President, to take on the risks that come with ensuring one of Sordland's most valuable energy companies continues to operate and grow?"

232.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
232.text: "Are you ready to make your government stronger?"

233.speaker: Player
233.text: "Don't you think there's a way we can ensure Gasom's growth without putting the government at risk?"

234.speaker: Player
234.text: "What kind of assurances can you provide that this will pay off in the long term, President Alphonso?"

235.speaker: Player
235.text: "I'm all for taking calculated risks. But we need to be sure that the benefits outweigh the potential losses."

236.speaker: Player
236.text: "Mr. Alphonso, are you suggesting that we should risk the treasury of Sordland for the growth of a single company?

237.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
237.text: "Not at all, Mr. President. I'm suggesting that supporting Gasom's growth could significantly contribute to Sordland's overall economic stability."

238.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
238.text: "Of course, Mr. President. I wouldn't propose a strategy that I didn't believe would be beneficial for both Gasom and Sordland."

239.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
239.text: "Gus, would you like to answer that?"

240.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
240.text: "Mr. President, in business, there are no guarantees. But I can assure you that we at Gasom are committed to doing everything in our power to ensure this deal pays off for Sordland."

241.speaker: Gus Manger
241.text: "Ewald is right. We're not talking about risking the economy. We're discussing an investment that has the potential to pay significant dividends for Sordland."

242.speaker: Gus Manger
242.text: "As someone who's been in the energy business for decades, I can tell you that this deal is solid."

243.speaker: Gus Manger
243.text: "Absolutely. I believe that by working together with Rizia, we can find a shared investment solution that promotes Gasom's growth while minimizing any potential risk to the government."

244.speaker: Gus Manger
244.text: "I can't give you a guarantee. But I can tell you that I trust President Alphonso, and I believe in this deal. Sometimes, you have to take a leap of faith."

247.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
247.text: "Mr. President, have you ever considered that the future of Sordland might rest not on avoiding risks, but about embracing them?"

248.speaker: Player
248.text: "I understand your point. However, the stakes are too high for us to gamble on uncertainty."

249.speaker: Player
249.text: "I have. And I believe that embracing uncertainty is a part of leadership. We must be bold in our decisions for the future of Sordland."

250.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
250.text: "That our greatest potential might lie not in the safety of what we know, but in the uncertainty of what we might discover?"

251.speaker: Player
251.text: "Liberalizing the energy market merely serves the interests of the wealthy elites. What we need is a comprehensive nationalization of the energy sector to ensure it serves the people, not profit."

252.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
252.text: "While I respect your perspective, Mr. President, I firmly believe that the power of the free market, coupled with appropriate regulation, can drive both progress and equity. It's not an 'us versus them' situation."

253.speaker: Gus Manger
253.text: "We must also consider the economic realities and global competitiveness. A balance between public ownership and market forces could be the key."

254.speaker: Player
254.text: "A thriving market economy is the engine of prosperity and innovation. I believe in Gasom's potential to compete and succeed under these principles."

255.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
255.text: "I'm glad we see eye to eye on this. With your support, I am confident that Gasom will be able to chart a prosperous future."

256.speaker: Gus Manger
256.text: "Your words are reassuring, Mr. President. Let's harness the power of the free market to elevate Gasom and, in turn, the entire Sordish economy."

258.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
258.text: "It's unfortunate we couldn't bridge our differences. Nonetheless, we respect your stance and value the time spent."

259.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
259.text: "Ready to make history together? Set our differences aside and work together for the energy independence of our nation?"

260.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
260.text: "Katarina Horten and Denis Stahler seem to be leading the group. It would be difficult to leave the way we came without causing trouble."

261.speaker: Player
261.text: "A helicopter might be the safer option."

262.speaker: Player
262.text: "I think we should face the crowd head-on."

264.speaker: Gus Manger
264.text: "Mr. President, I advise you to leave via helicopter just in case. I can stay back and update the crowd on the discussions today."

265.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
265.text: "I will give the order to ready it. We can fly to the Blue Mansion in Lachaven."

266.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
266.text: "That is your prerogative, Mr. President. Following the violent events of late, I heavily recommend against facing any crowd."

267.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
267.text: "Trust me, I know this place well. The only other way out is through a dangerous hilly terrain or the sewers."

270.speaker: Narrator
270.text: Everyone waited. The tense silence of the room stood in stark contrast to the buzz of the ever-growing crowd outside.

272.speaker: Gus Manger
272.text: "Amazing! I knew you two could make it work."

273.speaker: Gus Manger
273.text: "Before we conclude, Ewald, I've set aside time during this meeting for President Rayne to discuss concerns about Gasom's treatment of workers and its repercussions on Narbel."

274.speaker: Narrator
274.text: Alphonso nodded and looked at me.

275.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
275.text: "Do you have a proposal in mind, Mr. President?"

321.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
321.text: "I appreciate your visit today, and despite our differences, your willingness to meet with me is noted."

322.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
322.text: "Throughout my journey, I've held faith in collaborating with individuals who genuinely share my vision. The presence of the right allies amplifies our potential."

323.speaker: Gus Manger
323.text: "I'll leverage my Rizian contacts to finalize the deal."

324.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
324.text: "Our allies in the Golden Kingdom will step in where Sordland couldn't."

327.speaker: Player
327.text: "I'm not here for your approval, Alphonso. My priority is Gus and, more importantly, the workers."

328.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
328.text: "That sounds eerily like what Mr. Soll would say when things didn't go his way."

330.speaker: Player
330.text: "We must make decisions based on what is best for Sordland in the present moment."

331.speaker: Player
331.text: "Running the state is not like running your company Alphonso. You out of all people should know this."

333.speaker: Gus Manger
333.text: "The Labor Union and the Communist Party of Sordland have garnered significant support, capitalizing on the anxieties of the many Gasom workers concerned about their job security."

334.speaker: Gus Manger
334.text: "The worried workers will have no fears about job security thanks to this state intervention."

335.speaker: Gus Manger
335.text: "The Labor Union, along with the Communist Party of Sordland, has rallied substantial support from Gasom workers in Narbel, advocating for improved local conditions."

336.speaker: Player
336.text: "We need to address these concerns; they could jeopardize the administration."

337.speaker: Player
337.text: "Our duty is to listen and take action. That's the mandate granted to us by the public."

338.speaker: Player
338.text: "Gasom stands as a global energy powerhouse. It's only right they give back somewhat."

339.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
339.text: "Together, we might discover solutions beneficial to both parties."

341.speaker: Player
341.text: "I've wasted enough time to this. Time to depart."

342.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
342.text: "It's regrettable you feel this way, Mr. President."

343.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
343.text: "While sometimes people may not always recognize what's in their best interest."

345.speaker: Narrator
345.text: A member of the private security team entered the room, his face taut with urgency.

346.speaker: Player
346.text: "Look, gentlemen. My time is valuable, so let’s cut to the chase."

347.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
347.text: "Blunt. Must be the new way of doing things."

348.speaker: Player
348.text: "Don’t forget, the state stands above you all. Nothing may happen today, or next week, but the future is never certain."

349.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
349.text: "I have served Sordland all my life. It’s the people who voted for me, just like they did for you."

351.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
351.text: "I think it's time to call Mr. Montoro, Gus."

352.speaker: Gus Manger
352.text: "Thank you for making the trip and setting aside the time."
